incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected from private VPC egress gateway (apps-serving-prod) — error-rate spike from 00:03 UTC, paging on-call. Trigger: gateway_5xx_rate > 5% for 5m.
Maya K.: I’m on it. seeing a lot of 504/502 in the gateway logs. anyone else getting customer pings?
Jonah R.: getting several user reports of timeouts from org: acme-corp. Not full outage but degraded.
Priya S.: Confirmed — traces show requests timing out on egress to model-hosts in region eu-west-1 via private peering.
Lucas T.: grabbing gateway logs now — tail: ```
[2026-03-14T00:05:12Z] gw: upstream_connect_timeout, host=10.240.3.7:443, id=xyz
[2026-03-14T00:05:13Z] gw: 502 Bad Gateway, upstream=10.240.3.8:443
[2026-03-14T00:05:14Z] gw: 504 Gateway Timeout (pool exhausted)
```
Maya K.: running a quick curl from a test VM inside the private VPC: ```
curl -v https://model-host.internal/ping
* Connection timed out after 300000 ms
```
Jonah R.: tcpdump on egress gateway shows SYNs but a lot of retransmits; suspect NAT port exhaustion or conntrack limits.
Priya S.: checking node conntrack counters: `sudo conntrack -S | grep entries` shows 65534 entries on the gateway node (close to default nf_conntrack max).
Lucas T.: nice catch. kernel conntrack full leads to drop of new flows -> 5xx/timeouts. what pushed conntrack up? any sudden traffic pattern?
Maya K.: quick histogram of source ports shows many ephemeral ports in TIME_WAIT from the local proxy process. Could be internal retry storm or long-lived keepalives not reusing connections.
incident-bot: Incident severity: P2. Notified SRE rotation.
Jonah R.: mitigation plan: 1) raise conntrack max temporarily 2) rotate gateway node out of LB for drain 3) add temporary SNAT pool expansion if possible 4) root-cause investigation.
Priya S.: I can raise nf_conntrack on the flight: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` — will apply to the node and monitor.
Maya K.: go for it, Priya. also start draining one gateway instance so we can restart the process if needed.
Lucas T.: while Priya applies sysctl I’ll scale up the NAT gateway pool (k8s daemonset autoscale) and add a second egress IP range to increase ephemeral ports. That should reduce port reuse pressure.
Priya S.: applied `nf_conntrack_max=200000` on gateway-12. conntrack table freed up slowly as TIME_WAIT aged out. current entries down to ~110k.
Jonah R.: after pool expansion + conntrack increase, 5xx rate dropped from 6.8% to 1.2% over 3m. traces show new flows succeeding.
Maya K.: customer impact: Acme saw 30% of requests retried during spike window (00:03-00:11 UTC). We should prepare outbound comms.
Jonah R.: for immediate handoff: on-call (Maya) to SRE rotation (Lucas) for postmortem and capacity changes. I’ll update the incident channel with timelines.
Lucas T.: investigating root cause: looking at application logs, looks like a client-side retry loop from connector service `connector-proxy` that ramped up after upstream latencies increased — created many short-lived connections which exhaust ephemeral ports on the gateway NAT. Also found one peering route flap earlier in the morning correlating with spike.
Priya S.: also saw a handful of security-group rejections between gateway and peering appliance — some flows were being reset and retried, amplifying connection churn.
Maya K.: mitigation checklist done: `nf_conntrack_max` increased, rotated gateway instance + restarted proxy on drained node, scaled SNAT pool by adding 2 extra egress IPs, temporarily relaxed healthcheck aggressive requeues. 5xx rates back to baseline.
incident-bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INC-2026-1874, page history recorded.
Jonah R.: immediate post-incident actions: - add ~20% headroom to conntrack on all egress nodes - implement application-side connection pooling for connector-proxy - add alert on conntrack_utilization > 80% - tighten SG rules to avoid intermittent rejects causing retries - add smoother backoff to client retry loop
Lucas T.: I’ll own the conntrack sysctl rollout + alerting (SRE). Priya, can you file the peering engineering ticket for investigating the peering route flap with networking?
Priya S.: filing NETENG ticket now with packet captures and timestamps. will include tcpdump extracts and `ip route` snapshots.
Maya K.: customer comms: drafting note for Acme and any tenants with private peering noting short window of increased errors, mitigation steps taken, and planned follow-ups. cc: support.
Jonah R.: handoff: Maya -> Lucas for follow-up and root-cause. On-call remains Maya until 01:00 UTC then hand to next rotation.
Maya K.: leaving notes for postmortem: timeline with exact minute-by-minute; evidence (conntrack dumps, tcpdump, gateway logs); mitigations performed and rollback plan; follow-ups and owners.
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P3 at 00:35 UTC.
Lucas T.: action items created in the incident ticket with owners and eta: conntrack rollout (Lucas, 48h), connector-proxy connection pooling (platform: 2w), retry/backoff tuning (app teams: 1w), peering investigation (NetEng: 72h), customer email (Support: 4h).
Maya K.: any questions? otherwise I’ll close the paging handoff and update the runbook.
Jonah R.: all clear from me. thanks team. :heart:
Priya S.: closing my monitoring loop. will post packet captures to the ticket.
Maya K.: closing thread for active paging. I'll attach logs and steps to the ticket for the postmortem.
